quarterly_data.quarter: TOWA results briefing Q&A: FY2025 4Q Financial Results Briefing Q&A (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Orders and backlog, management (results briefing Q&A): Q4 orders fell from Q3 because some Taiwan Q4 projects were booked in Q3, and in Japan because the special Osaka University fusion-related order booked in Q3 was absent, along with some project timing shifts; management views the decline as temporary, with the order environment showing signs of recovery. Order backlog stands at just under half of this fiscal year's sales plan, with orders generally tracking expectations, though quarterly fluctuations remain possible.
quarterly_data.figure: Order backlog just under half of this fiscal year's sales plan

quarterly_data.quarter: TOWA results briefing Q&A: FY2025 4Q Financial Results Briefing Q&A (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: HBM, management (results briefing Q&A): memory investment including HBM has shifted from front-end expansion to assembly facility construction, with full-scale orders expected after factory completion later this year, though uncertainty remains (Middle East situation, construction schedules). HBM-related orders have already been secured ahead of schedule; customer forecasts for this fiscal year have been received and no sudden demand surge is expected, but capacity remains tight and additional orders could arise during the quarter. HBM investment has recently expanded beyond a limited number of customers and orders are expected to exceed the prior year's level. The view of demand for around 30-45 HBM units over several years remains broadly unchanged, while factory delays and power shortages in some countries continue to delay installation schedules. Unlike FY2023, when orders were concentrated in a short timeframe, HBM demand is expected to build more gradually, though it could temporarily concentrate depending on investment timing.
quarterly_data.figure: Demand for around 30-45 HBM units over several years (view broadly unchanged)

quarterly_data.quarter: TOWA results briefing Q&A: FY2025 4Q Financial Results Briefing Q&A (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Other demand, management (results briefing Q&A): strong demand continues among Taiwanese OSAT customers, although HBM-focused production is limiting supply of general-purpose memory; that demand should gradually recover once front-end capacity expansion stabilizes. FY2025's sharp increase in transfer molding equipment was driven mainly by power and analog semiconductors, including China-related demand; high-end compression molding remained focused on prototype projects, with mass-production investment expected to accelerate from this year into next year. China's domestic supply chain ecosystem remains tight, including consumer applications, and supply shortages persist, so solid China order trends are expected to continue for now.

quarterly_data.quarter: TOWA results briefing Q&A: FY2025 4Q Financial Results Briefing Q&A (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: PLP and MUF, management (results briefing Q&A): AI investment has so far centered on data centers, driving HBM demand; AI chip adoption is expected to expand to physical AI, smartphones and PCs, and growing demand for inference AI GPUs is increasing adoption of 500-600mm large-format panels to reduce costs. TOWA's vacuum-based MUF technology offers improved heat dissipation and lower cost through process simplification for high-heat AI semiconductors, supporting further PLP adoption. MUF's contribution in packages combining logic and memory was limited last year as projects were mainly prototypes, but evaluation of the technology is progressing and adoption is expected to expand as heat dissipation becomes a key issue for next-generation AI.

quarterly_data.quarter: TOWA results briefing Q&A: FY2025 4Q Financial Results Briefing Q&A (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New molding system INNOMS, management (results briefing Q&A): higher-density design gives approximately twice the productivity of the current PMC series within the same footprint, as strip-type equipment with a maximum supported size of 100 mm x 300 mm; the ability to reduce mass-production costs by about 50% is a key advantage; release film usage is 25% lower than TOWA's conventional models (consumables sales will decline, but the twofold productivity gain is expected to have a positive overall earnings impact). Targets: MAP packages for memory, QFN and RF modules, later areas needing compression molding for heat dissipation; both replacement demand and new investment. Margins are expected to exceed conventional compression molding equipment; the product is still at the prototype stage, has been introduced to some customers and is close to field evaluation; management confirmed customer evaluations and orders should begin this fiscal year.
quarterly_data.figure: About 2x productivity; mass-production cost about 50% lower; release film usage 25% lower; max 100 mm x 300 mm

quarterly_data.quarter: TOWA results briefing Q&A: FY2025 4Q Financial Results Briefing Q&A (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: This fiscal year's plan, management (results briefing Q&A): last year saw significant fluctuations due to factors including tariffs; this year's order and sales plan incorporates customer forecasts, mainly for HBM, and assumes relatively stable, more normalized trends. Higher sales should support profit growth, but strategic measures to strengthen market position are prioritized, so margin improvement is expected to be gradual; the mix between compression and transfer molding equipment is expected to be more balanced than last year (when mid-end transfer molding weighed on margins), supporting stable profitability. The Laser Front special project is not assumed to recur beyond this fiscal year.
